discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 250800
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
300 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Increasing clouds today which stick around through at least
  Friday. High temperatures will be in the 40s this week.

- A period of soaking rain arrives early Thursday morning and
  lingers through Friday (80-90% chance). A few snowflakes may
  mix in Thursday night.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 239 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

A cold start this morning with lows in the 20s will lead into 
another dry day today with highs slightly warmer than yesterday.
Highs will warm into the mid 40s with the help of some clearing
skies pushing in from the southeast before increasing clouds 
and a wetter period from Thanksgiving through Friday arrives. A 
negatively tilted trough pushes south into the northern Plains 
and Midwestern states from central Canada before becoming a 
more closed low feature and pushing northeastward through the 
Ohio River valley and into the northeastern portions of the 
CONUS later this week. Decent warm air advection associated with
this system for our area looks to keep precipitation mainly in 
the liquid form beginning Thursday early for our southern 
portions of the area and will quickly spread northward across 
the remainder of the area on Thursday.

Overnight Thursday into Friday morning a few snowflakes may mix
in but no snowfall accumulations are expected. However, 
rainfall totals for this system around an inch will be possible 
across the southern parts of the CWA with a gradual downward 
trend the further north you go with around a third of an inch 
for our southern MI counties. High temperatures over the next 
several days look to remain in the mid to upper 40s and lows 
mainly in the 30s. Dry weather returns this Saturday briefly 
with ridging in the wake of this first system moving through. 
Another system pushes eastward across the central CONUS and into
the region and looks to bring another bout of light rainfall 
Sunday into Monday morning. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 1222 AM EST Wed Nov 25 2026

A tightening pressure gradient today as low pressure develops
over the southeast US; in contrast to residing New England high 
pressure. High overcast skies this hour will drift north and 
expansive clearing is noted downstate. Clouds return later this 
TAF period as Atlantic moisture streams northward.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Andersen
AVIATION...Brown

spc.summary: Isolated severe storms capable of damaging winds and tornadoes or waterspouts appear possible over the Florida Keys and southern Florida peninsula today.
spc.text:
SPC AC 250559

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1159 PM CST Tue Nov 24 2026

   Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS THE FLORIDA
   KEYS AND FAR SOUTHERN FLORIDA PENINSULA...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated severe storms capable of damaging winds and tornadoes or
   waterspouts appear possible over the Florida Keys and southern
   Florida peninsula today.

   ...Synopsis...
   Late-evening water-vapor imagery reveals an upper low over the
   southern Plains drifting east/southeast towards the northern Gulf.
   An upper jet analyzed on the western flank of the trough will
   promote a more southeasterly track of the low over the next 24 hours
   into the eastern Gulf and eventually towards the Southeast Atlantic
   coast by 12 UTC Thursday. As this occurs, a diffuse surface low
   currently in place off the FL Keys will consolidate and intensify
   into an organized cyclone as it accelerates northeastward towards
   the Carolina coast through early Thursday morning. A vigorous
   low-level mass response is anticipated as the surface low
   strengthens, which will support the potential for organized
   thunderstorms, including isolated supercells, this afternoon across
   southern FL and possibly along the Carolina coast early Thursday. 

   ...Florida Keys/southern FL peninsula...
   As of 05:30 UTC, KBYX imagery already shows mid-level rotation in
   offshore convection within a relatively modest kinematic
   environment. Kinematic fields should improve through mid-day as the
   surface low intensifies and tracks across the southern FL peninsula.
   This will allow for a narrow warm sector (characterized by low 70
   dewpoints) to advance inland possibly as far north as the I-75
   corridor before the passage of the primary surface trough by around
   18-20 UTC. Within this warm sector, strong flow through the lowest
   1-2 km (possibly as strong as 40-50 knots per recent guidance) will
   support effective SRH values on the order of 150-250 m2/s2. Although
   the thermodynamic profile will be characterized by poor lapse rates,
   saturation through a deep layer and some degree of low-level
   heating/moistening through early afternoon should support adequate
   buoyancy for organized deep convection, including a few supercells
   capable of waterspouts/tornadoes. 

   The primary uncertainties will be to what degree stratiform
   precipitation modulates the inland progression of higher theta-e air
   near the surface, how storm mode will evolve within a weakly capped
   environment, and the spatial/temporal window for strong convection
   before the warm sector moves offshore. However, consensus among
   recent CAM ensembles suggests the tornado threat may be substantial
   enough to warrant 5% tornado risk probabilities along the coast and
   over the Keys.

   ...Carolina Coast...
   Forecast guidance suggests the surface low will advance northward
   and begin moving inland along the Carolina coast during the 9-12 UTC
   period early Thursday morning. Most guidance suggests a narrow warm
   sector will emerge along the coast as the low shifts north, and may
   support MLCAPE values as high as 250-500 J/kg. Intensifying
   low-level wind fields will support some potential for organized
   convection capable of producing damaging gusts and perhaps brief
   tornadoes before decaying and moving inland away from the better
   buoyancy.

   ..Moore/Dean.. 11/25/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 250622

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1222 AM CST Wed Nov 25 2026

   Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely Thursday.

   ...Synopsis...
   A strong surface pressure gradient will exist over the Mid Atlantic
   as a low moves from eastern NC into VA through 00Z. A deep upper low
   will pivot northeastward across the TN Valley with a leading wave
   moving northward well to the east over the Mid Atlantic.

   Very strong winds veering with height just above the cool boundary
   layer should support lift in the warm advection regime associated
   with the lead wave during the day from NC into VA and eventually
   into southern New England late. Substantial clouds and precipitation
   will limit destabilization potential, though elevated instability
   will support scattered thunderstorms.

   Elsewhere, an isolated lightning flash or two may occur over far
   western WA in association with an early-day shortwave trough with
   cool temperatures aloft, supporting minimal instability.

   ..Jewell.. 11/25/2026

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0105 AM CST Wed Nov 25 2026

   Valid 271200Z - 281200Z

   ...NO THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Thunderstorms are unlikely on Friday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low and associated large-scale trough will move quickly
   across the Northeast on Friday, with the primary cold front already
   off the East Coast. High pressure behind this system will reinforce
   stable conditions over much of the CONUS, and instability sufficient
   for thunderstorms appears unlikely to develop.

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
